Detailed Description

Hash functions for use with tommy_hashtable, tommy_hashdyn and tommy_hashlin.

This module provides hash functions designed for in-memory data structures. tommy_hash_u32 and tommy_strhash_u32 derive from a5hash32, while tommy_hash_u64 and tommy_strhash_u64 derive from a5hash.

Both variants are modified to improve adversarial collision resistance under the seeded collision-score metric described by Thomas Dybdahl Ahle in "Adversarial examples for fast hash functions": https://thomasahle.com/blog/adversarial-examples-for-hashes/ The original a5hash32 leaves one state lane independent of the seed, allowing distinct inputs of 9 to 16 bytes to collide for every seed. The original 64-bit a5hash can lose seed dependence during initialization, making specially crafted inputs collide more often across seeds than a uniform 64-bit hash. TommyDS changes initialization and mixing to address these weaknesses, so its hash values differ from the original algorithms.

Reversible integer hash functions are also provided for 32-bit and 64-bit keys.

tommy_hash_u32 is intended for 32-bit platforms and uses 32-bit operands with full 64-bit multiplication results. tommy_hash_u64 uses 64-bit operands with full 128-bit multiplication results. Both algorithms pass SMHasher3 tests.

Prefer the 64-bit version whenever possible, as it provides better resistance to collisions, particularly with specially crafted inputs. However, neither version is designed to resist deliberate collision attacks. If resistance to such attacks is required, use a dedicated hash function designed for that purpose.

All hash functions are intended for runtime in-memory use only and not for persistent storage, as hash compatibility across different versions of the library is not guaranteed. String and sized buffer hash functions produce identical results for 0-terminated strings.

◆ tommy_hash_u32()

TOMMY_API tommy_uint32_t tommy_hash_u32 ( tommy_uint32_t  init_val,
const void *  void_key,
tommy_size_t  key_len 
)

Hash function with a 32-bit result.

Derived from a5hash32 by Aleksey Vaneev from https://github.com/avaneev/a5hash

This algorithm is compact, fast on short inputs, and passes SMHasher3 tests.

Parameters
init_valInitialization value. Using a different initialization value, you can generate a completely different set of hash values. Use 0 if not relevant.
void_keyPointer to the data to hash. Must not be 0, even if key_len is 0.
key_lenSize of the data to hash.
Returns
The 32-bit hash value.
Note
This function is endianness independent and alignment independent. It produces identical hash results to tommy_strhash_u32 for 0-terminated strings. Compatibility across different versions of the library is not guaranteed: this hash is intended for in-memory runtime use only and not for persistent storage. It is non-cryptographic and is not designed to protect against malicious collision attacks.

◆ tommy_mulhash_u32()

tommy_uint32_t tommy_mulhash_u32 ( tommy_uint32_t  key)

Reversible 32-bit integer hash function using multiplications.

Implementation of the MurmurHash3 fmix32 finalizer by Austin Appleby, from https://github.com/aappleby/smhasher/blob/master/src/MurmurHash3.cpp

Parameters
keyThe 32-bit integer to hash.
Returns
The 32-bit hash value.
Note
Requires an architecture with fast 32-bit integer multiplication for good performance. See tommy_inthash_u32() for an alternative.

◆ tommy_mulhash_u64()

tommy_uint64_t tommy_mulhash_u64 ( tommy_uint64_t  key)

Reversible 64-bit integer hash function using multiplications.

Implementation of the SplitMix64 finalizer, from https://prng.di.unimi.it/splitmix64.c

Parameters
keyThe 64-bit integer to hash.
Returns
The 64-bit hash value.
Note
Requires an architecture with fast 64-bit integer multiplication for good performance. It is generally not recommended on 32-bit architectures, where these multiplications are expensive. Consider tommy_inthash_u64() instead.
